The belief: every component has to be declared in an NgModule, and even if small demos skip them, real apps need modules to group features, share components and lazy-load pages.
For most of Angular's history, that was simply how Angular worked. The

of an NgModule told the compiler which components, directives and pipes a template could use, and lazy loading meant a feature module. Years of tutorials, Stack Overflow answers and enterprise codebases are built on that model, and they're still out there. There's a true part too: NgModules aren't deprecated, many libraries still ship them, and the docs keep a full guide for them. What changed is that you no longer need them, for components or for structure.
A component is its own compilation context
The compiler still needs to know what every tag, attribute and pipe in a template refers to. A
